answers.In a sentence or two, what will it do fo: It gives credit card applications a score and automatically declines the ones below a cutoff.
answers.What kind of AI is it? If more than one: Gives a score, ranking, flag, category or forecast — e.g. a credit score, a fraud alert, a ranking of CVs, the likely cause of a problem
What information will it see or use? Tic: Information about people — clients, applicants, staff or anyone else: names, contact details, account and financial details, CVs — anything about someone who can be identified
answers.What happens with what it produces? If i: acts by itself within limits someone set, with no routine review
answers.What does it do when it acts?: Makes a yes-or-no decision — e.g. accepts or declines an application, signs something off
answers.Who ends up seeing or receiving what it: Clients or customers — including people applying to us
answers.Which of these does it help decide, if a: Whether to lend to someone, or on what terms
answers.How widely will it be used?: Several teams, the whole business, or every case of a kind (e.g. all applications)

expectNext: After I press Continue I think the tool will take me on to the 'Questions' step. It may ask a few more follow-up questions about my tool. Then there is a 'Confirm' step where I look over everything, and after that a 'Result'. The result should say whether the credit card scoring model can go ahead, and if not, what the credit team needs to do first. I expect the decision to come from the firm's written rules applied to my answers, not from the AI helper. I also expect that giving the same answers again would give the same result.
ticksMean: 'I've checked this answer' means I have read the AI helper's suggestion, compared it with what I know, and agree it is right. The tick is my sign-off. The helper only guessed from my description, and until I tick or change an answer it doesn't count and I can't continue. A tick does not make anything final. I can still change it before the decision. The ✓ marks on the earlier screen are different. They only show which topics my description touched on, not that anything is correct.
comment: As an HR person I could do about two-thirds of this form from the description alone. I had to answer "Not sure" on where the AI comes from, whether a mistake can be put right, and whether it replaces something, and the "firm's platform" question was the one I couldn't make sense of.
